title: Validation and application of a visual LAMP assay for Mpox diagnosis — Insights from clinical samples in Thailand☆
author: Jaroenram, Ongchanchai, et al.
materials: listed in Table 1. (Note that F3L gene is used in this protocol as a model target to demonstrate the feasibility of the assay.) Program the thermocycler according to the following setting: 94 °C for 2 min (initial denaturation), then 30 cycles of 94 °C denaturation (30 s), 60 °C annealing (45 s) and 75 °C extension (45 s). The final extension was carried out at 75 °C for an additional of 2 min. Confirm the presence of specific PCR product of 221 bp in size by agarose gel electrophoresis (Steps 23–29).Adjustment point: Lower or higher annealing temperatures may be used when optimizing conditions for different target sequences.

steps.title: Extract Monkeypox DNA from Swabs
steps.instruction: Isolate viral DNA from patient swabs and reconstitute in low‑salt water for downstream LAMP.

substeps.instruction: Collect nasopharyngeal or skin‑lesion swab samples and place them in viral transport medium (VTM).
Extract DNA from 150 µL of the VTM using the magLEAD® 12gC instrument with the MagDEADx SV kit, following the manufacturer’s manual.
Re‑suspend the eluate in 50 µL DNase‑/RNase‑free water; optionally assess concentration/quality by spectrophotometry, then store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare Recombinant Plasmid DNA
steps.instruction: Generate a pGEM‑T Easy plasmid containing the F3L target region for use as LAMP template.

substeps.instruction: Amplify the F3L gene fragment (221 bp) by PCR with primers F3 and B3: 94 °C 2 min; 30 cycles of 94 °C 30 s, 60 °C 45 s, 75 °C 45 s; final extension 75 °C 2 min. Verify size on agarose gel.
Ligate the PCR product into the pGEM‑T Easy vector at EcoRI‑HF sites and confirm ligation by agarose gel electrophoresis.
Transform the ligation mix into E. coli JM109 competent cells by heat shock at 42 °C, ice 2 min, add 900 µL LB, incubate 37 °C, 150 rpm for 90 min.
Plate the cells on IPTG/X‑Gal agar plates and incubate 37 °C for 16 h.
Pick white colonies, inoculate each into LB containing 100 µg/mL ampicillin, and grow 37 °C, 250 rpm for 16 h. Perform colony PCR with the same primers to confirm insertion.
Isolate plasmid DNA from positive colonies using the GeneJet Plasmid Miniprep kit.
Measure plasmid concentration at 260/280 nm by spectrophotometry and verify the insert by DNA sequencing.
Prepare ten‑fold serial dilutions of the plasmid in DNase‑/RNase‑free water to obtain working stocks of 50 000, 5 000, 500, 50, 5 and 0.5 copies/µL; store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Naked‑eye Color Observation
steps.instruction: Visually assess LAMP reaction colour after incubation.

substeps.instruction: Remove reaction tubes from the heat source and let them stand at room temperature for 1 min to allow full colour development.
Observe the tube colours (yellow = positive, purple = negative) and interpret according to the provided guideline.

steps.title: UV‑Vis Spectrophotometric Analysis (Optional)
steps.instruction: Measure absorbance of LAMP products to objectively confirm colour change.

substeps.instruction: Turn on the NanoDrop® spectrophotometer, select the UV‑Vis (300–700 nm) mode, and perform a blank measurement with DNase‑/RNase‑free water.
Pipette 2 µL of the LAMP product onto the pedestal, form a dome, lower the sampling arm onto the sample, and start the measurement.
After the reading, lift the pedestal and clean the surface with a Kimwipe, avoiding direct contact.
Compare the obtained absorption spectrum with the reference (absence of a 430 nm peak indicates a negative sample).

steps.title: Agarose Gel Electrophoresis of LAMP Products
steps.instruction: Separate LAMP amplicons on a 2 % agarose gel and visualise under UV.

substeps.instruction: If not analysing immediately, store the LAMP product at –20 °C to 4 °C.

Prepare a 2 % (w/v) agarose gel in 1 × TAE: dissolve 2 g agarose in 100 mL 1 × TAE (microwave), pour into a casting tray with a comb, allow to solidify, then remove the comb. Use slightly excess TAE to compensate for evaporation.
Place the gel in an electrophoresis chamber with the comb side facing the anode (‑) and add enough 1 × TAE to cover the gel.
Mix 5 µL of each LAMP product with 1 µL 6 × DNA loading buffer, load the mixtures into the wells.
Run the gel at 100–120 V for ~30 min until the tracking dye reaches the bottom of the gel.
Stain the gel in 0.1 % SERVA G solution for 5 min, then de‑stain in distilled water for 10 min.
Visualise the bands under UV light and interpret the ladder‑like pattern as a positive result according to the guideline.

steps.title: Real‑time Turbidity Measurement (Optional)
steps.instruction: Monitor LAMP amplification continuously using a Loopamp Real‑time Turbidimeter.

substeps.instruction: Run the LAMP reactions in the LA‑500 device; the instrument records turbidity every 6 s by detecting magnesium pyrophosphate precipitation and displays a real‑time amplification curve.
Interpret the curve: a rising turbidity curve indicates a positive sample, while a flat curve indicates no amplification (negative).
Record the data by printing directly from the device or by manually noting the displayed values.
After the run, the LA‑500 automatically heats the reaction block to inactivate the enzyme; dispose of the used tubes according to laboratory safety procedures.
